title: The Hidden Difference Between Good and Bad Debt

beats.say: A $3,000 credit card balance will quietly double to $6,000 in just three years.
beats.visual: A close-up of a person's hands cutting a dark credit card in half with heavy metal shears under moody, dark lighting.

beats.say: That's high interest consumer debt. But the wealthy use a completely different type of debt to build empires.
beats.visual: A low-angle shot of a tall modern office building at night with warm office lights glowing inside.

beats.say: We're always told that all debt is bad. That basic rule keeps you safe, but it keeps you broke.
beats.visual: A closed dusty leather-bound ledger on a dark mahogany desk, illuminated by a single spotlight.

beats.say: High interest consumer debt is financial cancer. At 24% interest, your balance grows faster than you can earn.
beats.visual: A close-up of a rusty water valve slowly dripping water onto a dark concrete floor.

beats.say: Paying a typical 2% minimum on that card keeps you trapped in debt for over 15 years.
beats.visual: An extreme close-up of an hourglass with black sand slowly running down in a dimly lit room.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions. Debt is not inherently evil; it's just a tool, like a scalpel.
beats.visual: Hands in the shadow carefully placing a clean, silver surgical scalpel onto a sterile steel tray.

beats.say: In the hands of a trained surgeon, it saves lives. In the hands of a child, it's deadly.
beats.visual: A clean, empty wooden table in a minimalist modern room with soft cinematic side-lighting.

beats.say: If you can secure low-interest debt to buy an asset yielding a higher return, you pocket the difference.
beats.visual: A wide cinematic shot of a modern residential apartment building at dusk, warm interior lights.

beats.say: This is productive leverage. It's how smart investors buy cash flowing assets with almost none of their own money.
beats.visual: A close-up of hands turning a heavy brass key inside an old rustic wooden door.

beats.say: Learning to spot the difference is how you scale. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking down a quiet library aisle lined with tall bookshelves.

beats.say: Because without understanding this crucial line, you'll always look at a balance sheet and wonder why...
beats.visual: A rainy window pane at night with city streetlights blurred into soft bokeh in the background.

caption: All debt is not created equal. Here is how the wealthy use leverage to build empires while consumer debt keeps others trapped. 📉
description: An explanation of the difference between high-interest consumer debt and low-interest productive debt. Learn how to identify when debt is a destructive trap versus a powerful wealth-building tool.
first_comment: What is the worst piece of debt advice you have ever been given?

facts.claim: At 24% interest, debt doubles every 3 years.
facts.basis: Rule of 72: at 24% debt doubles every 3 years.

facts.claim: Paying a 2% minimum on a $3,000 credit card at 24% keeps you trapped in debt for over 15 years.
facts.basis: $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25): 183 months (~15 years).
